--- title: "Covariance, Correlation, and Scatterplots" subtitle: "PSYC 6019-A01 / PSYC 6022-A01
2026-11-06 | Lab 11" author: "Jess Helmer" footer: "[jhelmer3.github.io/PSYC6019-2026](https://jhelmer3.github.io/PSYC6019-2026/)" format: revealjs: code-link: true slide-number: true code-line-numbers: false theme: ../../gt-theme.scss width: 1200 execute: echo: true dpi: 600 freeze: auto knitr: opts_chunk: dev: svg --- ## Outline - Correlation - Scatterplots - Scatterplot matrices ::: {.cell} ::: # Correlation ## Correlation So far, we've been talking about continuous outcomes as predicted by different **categorical** variables. But the world is not limited to categorical predictors! Today, we are going to talk about estimating associations between two continuous variables by examining their **correlation**. ## Correlation Correlation is a measure of the **linear association** between two continuous variables. Is a standardized version of **covariance**. ## Covariance Covariance is an unstandardized index of the linear relationship between two continuous variables. $$ s_{xy} = \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^N (x_i - \bar{x}) (y_i - \bar{y}) }{N - 1} $$ ::: subpoint ○ $x_i$: an observation of $x$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $\bar{x}$: sample mean of $x$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $y_i$: an observation of $y$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $\bar{y}$: sample mean of $y$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $N$: sample size ::: *The deviations of each $x_i$ from its mean and the deviations of each $y_i$ from its mean, multiplied together, summed up, and divided by the sample size minus one.* ## Covariance Visually Examples of positive, zero, and negative covariance: ::: {.cell layout-ncol="3" layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=384} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-2.svg){fig-align='center' width=384} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-3.svg){fig-align='center' width=384} ::: ::: ## Correlation It's tricky to numerically interpret a covariance, because it is in a combination of x and y's units. Correlation standardizes covariance down to a single scale. $$ r_{xy} = \frac{s_{xy}}{s_{x} s_{y}} $$ ::: subpoint ○ $s_{xy}$: covariance between $x$ and $y$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $s_x$: sample standard deviation of $x$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $s_y$: sample standard deviation of $y$ ::: We standardize covariance into correlation just by dividing by the two variables' standard deviations! ## Correlation It's tricky to numerically interpret a covariance, because it is in a combination of x and y's units. Correlation standardizes covariance down to a single scale. $$ r_{xy} = \frac{s_{xy}}{s_{x} s_{y}} = \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^N (x_i - \bar{x}) (y_i - \bar{y}) }{\sqrt{\sum_{i = 1}^N (x_i - \bar{x})^2} \sqrt{\sum_{i = 1}^N (y_i - \bar{y})^2}}$$ Bounded from $[-1, \ 1]$ ::: subpoint ○ $r_{xy} = -1$: strong negative correlation (when $x$ increases, $y$ tends to decrease) ::: ::: subpoint ○ $r_{xy} = 0$: no correlation ($x$ increasing doesn't provide information about $y$) ::: ::: subpoint ○ $r_{xy} = 1$: strong positive correlation (when $x$ increases, $y$ tends to increase) ::: ## Covariance in R `cov(x, y = NULL, use = "everything", method = "pearson")` ::: subpoint ○ `x` = numeric vector or dataframe ::: ::: subpoint ○ `y` = if `x` is a numeric vector, can specify `y` as a numeric vector ::: ::: subpoint ○ `use` = how to handle missing (`NA`) values ::: ::: subpoint ○ `method` = which type of coefficient to compute ::: ## Covariance in R Need to `select()` down just to variables of interest. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column .fragment width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(palmerpenguins) penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cov() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm NA NA body_mass_g NA NA ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .fragment width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cov(use = "complete.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 197.7318 9824.416 body_mass_g 9824.4161 643131.077 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Correlation in R `cor(x, y = NULL, use = "everything", method = "pearson")` ::: subpoint ○ `x` = numeric vector or dataframe ::: ::: subpoint ○ `y` = if `x` is a numeric vector, can specify `y` as a numeric vector ::: ::: subpoint ○ `use` = how to handle missing (`NA`) values ::: ::: subpoint ○ `method` = which type of coefficient to compute ::: ## Correlation in R :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1 NA body_mass_g NA 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "complete.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1.0000000 0.8712018 body_mass_g 0.8712018 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Handling `NA`s `cov()` and `cor()` have different options for what to do if missing values (`NA`s) are present ::: subpoint ○ `"everything"` = use all values: if one is `NA`, result will be `NA` ::: ::: subpoint ○ `"all.obs"` = use all values: if one is `NA` throw an error ::: ::: subpoint ○ `"complete.obs"` = delete rows with any `NA` values at all: if no rows remaining, throw an error ::: ::: subpoint ○ `"na.or.complete"` = delete rows with any `NA` values at all: if no rows remaining, result will be `NA` ::: ::: subpoint ○ `"pairwise.complete.obs"` = for each pair of variables, delete rows if either of the pairs is `NA`: may result in correlations being computed on different sample sizes ::: ## Handling `NA`s :::: {.columns style="font-size:90%"} ::: {.column width="33%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "everything") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1 NA body_mass_g NA 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "all.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `cor()`: ! missing observations in cov/cor ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "complete.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1.0000000 0.8712018 body_mass_g 0.8712018 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: :::: {.columns style="font-size:90%"} ::: {.column width="17%"} ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "na.or.complete") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1.0000000 0.8712018 body_mass_g 0.8712018 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` flipper_length_mm body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 1.0000000 0.8712018 body_mass_g 0.8712018 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="17%"} ::: :::: ## Scatterplots ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-20-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + labs(y = "Body Mass", x = "Flipper Length") + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ## Scatterplots ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-22-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} r <- cor(penguins$flipper_length_mm, penguins$body_mass_g, use = "complete.obs") penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)) + geom_point() + annotate(geom = "text", label = round(r, 2), x = mean(penguins$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = T), y = max(penguins$body_mass_g, na.rm = T)) + labs(y = "Body Mass", x = "Flipper Length") + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ## Scatterplots :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} If there are lots of datapoints, may want to take down the `alpha` for clearer results. E.g., with the `tidyverse` `diamonds` dataset. ::: ::: {.column .fragment width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-24-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x = carat, y = price)) + geom_point() + labs(y = "Price", x = "Carat") + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_currency()) + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Scatterplots :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} If there are lots of datapoints, may want to take down the `alpha` for clearer results. E.g., with the `tidyverse` `diamonds` dataset. ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-26-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} diamonds |> ggplot(aes(x = carat, y = price)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.025, shape = 16, size = 2) + labs(y = "Price", x = "Carat") + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_currency()) + guides(x = guide_axis(cap = T), y = guide_axis(cap = T)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Scatterplot Matrices ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-28-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=480} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # install.packages("GGally") penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) |> GGally::ggpairs() ``` ::: ::: ## Scatterplot Matrices ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Plot ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lab_12_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-30-1.svg){fig-align='center' width=576} ::: ::: ### Code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g, bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm) |> GGally::ggpairs() ``` ::: ::: ## Lab 12 Activity

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
